misconceptions: Assuming parallel and analogy mean the same thing whenever both appear relevant.

words.sense: a comparison deliberately used to explain one subject through another
misconceptions: Assuming parallel and analogy mean the same thing whenever both appear relevant.

semantic_axes.description: A parallel is a shared pattern between situations; an analogy is a comparison employed to make an idea easier to understand.

chains.frame: Which word best describes the connection Asha noticed between two work experiences?

beats.text: Asha noticed that her first job and her cousin’s began with difficult training followed by help from patient mentors.
beats.decisive_clue: two actual experiences follow the same sequence
beats.reason: Two actual experiences follow the same sequence is the strongest evidence for parallel here.

beats.text: Their jobs were in different cities and several years apart.
beats.decisive_clue: two actual experiences follow the same sequence; different dates and cities does not change that
beats.reason: Distance does not erase the meaningful matching pattern across the two experiences.

chains.feedback_short: Two actual experiences follow the same sequence still decides; the later detail does not change that.
chains.feedback_deep: Parallel means a close similarity in pattern between distinct situations; analogy means a comparison deliberately used to explain one subject through another. Distance does not erase the meaningful matching pattern across the two experiences.
chains.contrast_rule: Parallel: two events follow the same pattern; analogy: comparison clarifies an unfamiliar idea.

hints.attention: Look at the sequence in each experience.
hints.axis: A parallel is a shared pattern between situations; an analogy is a comparison employed to make an idea easier to understand.
hints.contrast: Parallel: two events follow the same pattern; analogy: comparison clarifies an unfamiliar idea.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Minh’s comparison while teaching budgeting?

beats.text: To explain budgeting, Minh drew three buckets: rent fills the first, food the second, and savings get what remains.
beats.decisive_clue: bucket comparison is used to explain money allocation
beats.reason: Bucket comparison is used to explain money allocation is the strongest evidence for analogy here.

beats.text: He labelled each bucket and used them to show why spending order matters.
beats.decisive_clue: bucket comparison is used to explain money allocation; further evidence: labelled buckets clarify the order of payments
beats.reason: The extra explanation confirms the buckets are an illustrative tool for understanding a different idea.

chains.contrast_rule: Parallel: two events follow the same pattern; analogy: comparison clarifies an unfamiliar idea.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Hyejin’s wardrobe comparison?

beats.text: Hyejin compared her friend’s crowded inbox to an overstuffed wardrobe to explain why messages needed sorting into categories.
beats.decisive_clue: familiar wardrobe is used to explain email organization
beats.reason: Familiar wardrobe is used to explain email organization is the strongest evidence for analogy here.

beats.text: She pointed out that clothes and emails differ greatly, but her friend then understood the sorting idea.
beats.decisive_clue: different objects still clarify the organizing principle
beats.reason: The objects need not be alike in every respect; the comparison serves an explanatory purpose.

chains.feedback_short: Different objects still clarify the organizing principle makes analogy the better choice.
chains.feedback_deep: Parallel means a close similarity in pattern between distinct situations; analogy means a comparison deliberately used to explain one subject through another. The objects need not be alike in every respect; the comparison serves an explanatory purpose.
chains.contrast_rule: Parallel: two events follow the same pattern; analogy: comparison clarifies an unfamiliar idea.
